initial_finding: shared_funder_overlap_block reported MISMATCH via exact list-equality (p_rows == u_rows) on a GROUP BY source ORDER BY shared_creators DESC LIMIT 200 query with NO secondary sort key.

root_cause_investigation.duplicate_key_theory_disproven: Checked production (signature,source,destination) uniqueness directly: 5223038 total rows == 5223038 distinct triples, zero duplicates. The unified-merge helper (INSERT OR IGNORE with UNIQUE(signature,source,destination)) does not silently drop any real rows.
root_cause_investigation.full_unified_rebuild_verified: Rebuilt the complete HOT+COLD union (replacement_main.db id<=6648855 + all 41 cold_segments) into an isolated file-backed table: 3487386 HOT + 1735652 COLD = 5223038 total, 5223038 distinct triples, 0 duplicate collapse -- exact match to production row count.
root_cause_investigation.conclusion: The single differing row on each side has the IDENTICAL shared_creators value (64) -- a genuine SQL ORDER BY tie at the LIMIT 200 boundary. With no secondary sort key, SQLite resolves ties using internal row/page order, which legitimately differs between productions live B-tree layout and the freshly rebuilt P5A tables. This is a query-design artifact of the validation script (and would equally affect the real endpoint if called twice against production with a physical reorganization like VACUUM in between), NOT a data-completeness or migration defect.

verdict_basis: 199/200 exact match, 1/200 boundary tie with identical value, 0 data loss, 0 duplicates, exact row-count match on full 5.2M-row union
recommendation_for_endpoint_code: Not required for P5A. If exact reproducibility of tied ranks is ever needed, add a secondary ORDER BY source ASC tie-break to the shared_funder_overlap_block query in main.py -- purely a determinism nicety, not a correctness bug.
